why: Changing positions and movement can provide comfort and help you participate, but there is no single perfect posture or required break schedule.

slides.title: More Than One Good Position
slides.content: Bodies can use many positions. A posture is not automatically harmful because it looks different from an idealized picture.

slides.title: Comfort Can Change
slides.content: Staying in one position may feel uncomfortable for some people. A position change or brief movement can be a useful option—not a rule everyone must follow.

slides.title: Choose a Workable Dose
slides.content: Try alternating tasks, positions, or movement breaks at intervals that fit your symptoms, work, and goals.

slides.title: Build Capacity Too
slides.content: Variety can help with comfort, while gradually building strength, endurance, and confidence can support longer-term participation.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: Choose one point in your day to change position or move briefly. Notice whether it changes comfort or function, then adjust the plan.
slides.resourceLabel: Read the IASP back-pain education fact sheet

title: Use movement variety as an option
